key_insight: SVR learns to self-verify its own answers and use that signal to stop early when confident, reducing test-time compute without relying on external feedback.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical adaptive inference strategy for reasoning systems, letting harder inputs get more refinement while easy inputs finish with fewer turns.
method: Multi-turn reinforcement learning with GRPO on fixed-horizon trajectories
Each turn predicts a solution plus a discrete verdict and confidence score
Retain the answer only if verdict = Correct and confidence clears a threshold; otherwise continue refinement
evidence_signal: On seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3.5-2B, SVR reports 0.563 macro-average accuracy with 2.99 inference turns on average.
watch_item: The approach depends on well-calibrated self-verification and thresholding, so miscalibration could cause premature stopping or unnecessary extra compute.
paper_title: SVR: Self-Verifying Refinement via Joint Verdict-Confidence Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Test-Time Compute
